solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some space reserved for tree

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a garden is set aside for planting a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for tree' as the definition, but 'for' cannot stand in for a tree; it is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so the word names a kind of tree.

clue.text: Large fish found in Scottish town

parts.note: large means big
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A huge fish has been landed in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: BIGGAR is a small town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggar is a market town in the Scottish Borders region of Lanarkshire.

clue.text: This chicken's a goner — hit when going round area at maximum velocity

indicators.note: the word for hit wraps itself around the other pieces, as if circling them

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them
a patch is a small area of ground
c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, the greatest velocity possible

explanation.surface: A doomed chicken is struck while being chased around a yard at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal; c for the speed of light is a physics convention, the top velocity anything can reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatchcock is a bird split open and flattened for grilling, so it is certainly finished as a living fowl.

clue.text: Medical establishment? Class one 'less than wholly pleasant'

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for pleasant is not given complete: its final letter is cut off

parts.note: pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A sniffy remark that a medical centre's class is only partly agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place where patients receive outpatient treatment, an establishment of medicine.

clue.text: Round trip perhaps getting cut

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a mission is one kind of trip, as in a space mission

explanation.surface: A round trip, maybe, is being shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, a cut made from a text or list.

clue.text: Fine intelligent king got rid of

indicators.note: says the word for king is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: a thinking person is an intelligent one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever monarch has been dismissed, and that is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine thread or fine lines are slender ones, so fine is a synonym of slim or narrow.

clue.text: Adore material produced by poet

parts.note: to adore is to love
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Someone loves the fabric a poet has made.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was a seventeenth-century Cavalier poet, author of 'To Althea, from Prison'.

clue.text: Preaches in Home Counties, more sins being about

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric lectures about sin growing in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England; 'being about' gives RMONISES.
explanation.definitionFit: To sermonise is to deliver a moralising lecture, much like a preacher in the pulpit.

clue.text: Firm established by shoemaker, not at home

indicators.note: not says the letters for at home are removed

parts.note: St Crispin is the patron saint of shoemakers, and by extension a name for a cobbler
in means at home

explanation.surface: A company set up by a cobbler who is never in.
explanation.definitionFit: Crisp lettuce or crisp snow is firm and brittle, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Spooner's beautiful maiden sounded like a cow swelling inside the body

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words swap

parts.note: a nymph is a beautiful young woman
a cow lows, so it lowed

explanation.surface: A lovely girl mooed, and that's a lump inside you.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland of the lymphatic system is a small swelling in tissue that filters lymph fluid.

clue.text: Trendy seaside place British avoided

indicators.note: the letter for British is shunned, so it is left out

parts.note: Brighton is a resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A fashionable coastal resort that Brits stay away from.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort town on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is slang for fashionably progressive or up to date, near enough to trendy.

clue.text: Ray, a boy said to smile

indicators.note: said tells us the word for a boy is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a son is a boy
to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: Ray, a lad, is supposed to grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a boy's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of sunlight is a single ray of light from our star.

clue.text: Woman with worry about being short

indicators.note: about turns the shortened word round
the word for worry lacks its final letter

parts.note: to harass is to worry or pester

explanation.surface: A woman anxious about her small stature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short' trims HARASS to HARAS, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: A place noted for its transforming power?

definitions.text: A place noted for its transforming power?

parts.words: A place noted for its transforming power?
parts.note: a site in the electricity grid where transformers step voltage down for local supply

explanation.definitionFit: Electrical transformers there change the voltage of the supply, so it literally transforms power.

clue.text: Leader that is getting newspaper into row

indicators.note: into says the other pieces go inside the word for row

parts.note: a chain is a row of linked things
IE (id est) means that is
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A leader is getting a newspaper into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line of things: CHAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, its leader.

clue.text: People who do what they like to make a toilet available again?

definitions.text: People who do what they like

parts.note: a toilet that was occupied becomes free again
the gents is a men's lavatory

explanation.surface: Independent people who would vacate a lavatory for others.
explanation.walkthrough: The GENTS is the British name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Free agents are independent people not bound by obligations to anyone, so they act as they please.

clue.text: Team of potential world-beaters? Non!

indicators.note: potential says the letters are not yet in their final form, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Could these be champions of the world? No, says a sceptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges WORLDBEATERS NON. BOLTON WANDERERS is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolton Wanderers is a football club from Lancashire, England, so it is a team.

clue.text: Withdraw from young hooligan getting pepped up

parts.note: to withdraw from a place is to leave it
a ned is a young Scottish hooligan

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a young thug, which gives one a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: NED is Scottish slang for a young hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavened bread is raised by yeast, and figuratively leavened means enlivened or lightened.

clue.text: It could be Copenhagen's well-loved piece of music

definitions.meaning: Copenhagen was the Duke of Wellington's mount at Waterloo, a battle steed
a familiar, much performed classic that orchestras play over and over

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copenhagen' suggests the Danish capital, but it was the Duke of Wellington's horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Copenhagen carried Wellington in battle; a hackneyed, popular concert favourite is also called by this name.

clue.text: Author in cutter in Scottish water

indicators.note: the second in places the cutter inside the Scottish river

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river
a hacker is one who cuts or chops

explanation.surface: A writer aboard a small boat on a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' suggests a boat, but it is one who hacks.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was a Victorian novelist, writer of Vanity Fair.

clue.text: Leaders of expedition desperately trapped under boat screamed

indicators.note: in a down clue, the opening letters sit below the boat

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Explorers stuck beneath a boat cried out in desperation.
explanation.definitionFit: To yawl is a dialect verb meaning to howl or yowl, so yawled means cried out loud.

clue.text: Scotsman in endless pain? Not I

indicators.note: Not says the letter I is taken away
the word for pain loses its last letter

parts.note: anguish is severe pain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot in never-ending pain denies it is him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' makes ANGUIS, and 'Not I' removes the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a typical Scottish male name, so it can stand for a Scotsman.

clue.text: Physicist finding gravitational constant on top of mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece is placed above the mountain

parts.note: G is the symbol for the gravitational constant
the Eiger is a peak in the Swiss Alps

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers a law of gravity atop a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Geiger was the German scientist who co-invented the radiation counter named after him.

clue.text: The man put in new robot for old instrument

indicators.note: put in says the pronoun is inserted into the rearranged letters
new says the letters are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: he refers to the man

explanation.surface: A man is placed in a newly built robot to make an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' yields TORBO and 'put in' inserts the pronoun after its first letter; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorbo is a large bass lute of the seventeenth century, an early stringed instrument.

clue.text: It's right for a prince, as you may say, to be boisterous

indicators.note: as you may say means the word is spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: something fit for a prince is royal

explanation.surface: It is proper for a prince, people might say, to be rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: To roil is to churn or be turbulent, like rough water, hence to be wild and boisterous.

clue.text: Showing more emotion when there's little support

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more tearful when they get little help.
explanation.definitionFit: Weepier is the comparative of weepy, more tearful, more inclined to cry.

clue.text: Recruit losing heart is put down

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for recruit is dropped

parts.note: to raise an army is to recruit it

explanation.surface: A demoralised new soldier is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recruit' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to raise troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Rase is a variant spelling of raze, to demolish or level a building to the ground.

clue.text: Giving away too much with respect to children

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Parents spoil their children by handing out too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To overissue is to put out more shares, notes or stock than is allowed, an excess of distribution.

clue.text: Weak son must first get the muscular strength

indicators.note: says the word the comes before the other pieces

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A feeble son has to build up muscle first.
explanation.definitionFit: Thews are muscles or sinews, and by extension bodily strength or brawn.
